parts.text: A student investigates the cooling of water in different sized beakers. He uses the apparatus shown in Fig. 1.1. Beaker A and beaker B have graduations as shown in Fig. 1.1. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Record room temperature θ R shown on the thermometer in Fig. 1.1. θ R = .................................................... °C [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student pours an estimated volume of 75 cm 3 of hot water into beaker A. He uses the scale on the beaker as a guide. He puts the thermometer into the water in beaker A and records, in Table 1.1, the temperature θ at time t = 0. He records, in Table 1.1, the temperature of the water in beaker A every 30 s. The student repeats the procedure for beaker B. His readings are shown in Table 1.1. Suggest one possible source of inaccuracy in the procedure, even if it is carried out carefully. ................................................................................................................................................... ............................................................................................................................................. parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) Calculate the average cooling rate x for beaker B. Use the readings for beaker B in Table 1.1 and the equation x = θ 0 – θ 180 T where T = 180 s and θ 0 and θ 180 are the temperatures of the water in beaker B at t = 0 and t = 180 s. Include the unit for the cooling rate. x = ......................................................... [2]
